paragraphs.text: 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

General Manager of its own to act as liaison with the other Party for the Site (each a "General Manager") who shall bear sole responsibility for bookkeeping and business operations of the Site on a day-today basis. Each General Manager shall have the authority to make and convey decisions on behalf of each Party and to be the liaison with the other Party for all production and Content matters.
6. Exclusivity.

6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
The Company hereby grants to HDI a non-exclusive, limited, non-transferable license to use the Company's "Deerskin" trademarks, service

marks, and logos (collectively, "Marks") solely for the purpose of carrying out its obligations under this Agreement. Except as provided herein, no licenses of the Company's Marks are granted or implied under this Agreement.
6.2 The Company retains the right to establish a web site on the Internet for the purpose of offering closeout
merchandise which may be identified as "Deerskin" branded products, if such is the case.

6.3 During the term of this Agreement and for a period of two years after the expiration date of this Agreement, HDI shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet from which products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) are offered for sale to consumers on the Internet.
7. Cross-Promotions.

7.1 Joint Efforts. The Parties agree to cross-promote one another's products through the use of their respective customer e-mail lists on a reciprocal and equitable basis. The Parties specifically agree that the form, content and design of any and all advertisements or promotional materials featuring the other Party or such Party's products shall continue to be developed by or on behalf of such Party and shall be subject to such Party's final approval. The Parties agree further that any promotions or advertisements involving the use of a Party's customer e-mail list by the other Party shall be subject to the prior approval of such Party.

7.2 Mutual Covenants as to Advertisements. The Parties hereby covenant and agree that their respective marketing and advertising efforts provided for herein shall at all times comply with all applicable laws rules and regulations and will

not contain any material which is obscene, threatening, fraudulent, harassing, libelous, infringing of third party intellectual property rights, otherwise illegal or, in the reasonable judgment of the Party required to display or transmit the advertisement, offensive.
8. Confidentiality.

8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the Company, HDI shall maintain the strict confidentiality and shall not disclose to any third party the existence of, or terms and conditions of this Agreement. In addition, HDI, in performing the Services for the Company hereunder, may have access to or be exposed to, directly or indirectly, Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information of the Company in oral, graphic, written, electronic or machine readable form (hereinafter collectively referred to as "Confidential Information"). Confidential Information shall not include information which can be demonstrated:
(a) to have been rightfully in the possession of HDI from a source other than the Company prior to the time of disclosure of said information to HDI hereunder ("Time of Receipt");
(b) to have been in the public domain prior to the Time of Receipt;

(c) to have become part of the public domain after the Time of Receipt by a publication or by any other means except an unauthorized act or omission or breach of this Agreement on the part of HDI, its employees, or agents; or (d) to have been supplied to HDI after the Time of Receipt by a third party who is under no obligation to the
Company to maintain such information in confidence.

8.2 HDI Obligations. All Confidential Information of the Company shall be held in strict confidence by HDI and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of the Company, except as may be required by law. HDI shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for Confidential Information, including measures at least as strict as those HDI uses to protect its own Confidential Information.

8.3 Company's Obligations. The Company acknowledges that it may receive confidential information of HDI relating to its technical, marketing, product and/or business affairs. All such confidential information of HDI shall be-held in strict confidence by the Company and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of HDI, except as may be required by law. The Company shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for such confidential information of HDI, including measures at least as strict as those the Company uses to protect its own Confidential Information.
9. Warranties.

(a) Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation; (2) it has the full right power and authority to enter into, and to perform the obligations contemplated in this Agreement, and the person signing on its behalf has the full right,

power and authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of the Party; (3) this Agreement constitutes a legal valid and binding obligation of the Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; and (4) the execution of this Agreement will not conflict in any way with any pre-existing agreements or understandings of the Party with any person or entity.

(b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date
10. General Provisions.

10.1 Notices. Any notice under this Agreement will be in writing and delivered by personal delivery, express courier, confirmed facsimile, or certified or registered mail, return receipt requested and will be deemed given upon personal delivery, one (1) day after deposit with express courier, upon confirmation of receipt of facsimile or five (5),days after deposit in the mail. Notices will be sent to a Party at its address set forth above or such other address as that Party may specify in writing pursuant to this Section.

10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative. Neither Party shall have any right, power or authority to enter into any agreement for or on behalf of, or to assume or create any obligation, liability, or responsibility on behalf of the other.

This Agreement will not be construed to create or imply an association, joint venture, co-ownership, or partnership between the Parties or to impose any partnership obligation or liability upon either Party.

10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.

10.4 Waiver of Breach. The failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Agreement shall not be deemed or construed to be a waiver of any such provisions, or in any way to affect the right of any Party hereto to thereafter enforce each and every provision of this Agreement. No waiver of any breach of any provisions of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in writing and executed by the Party against which enforcement of such waiver is sought; and no waiver of any such breach shall be construed or deemed to be a waiver of any other or subsequent breach.

10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
10.6 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is declared invalid or otherwise determined to be unenforceable
for any reason, such provision shall be deemed to be severable from the remaining provisions of this Agreement, which shall otherwise remain in full force and effect.
10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

10.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement is the complete and exclusive agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding any prior agreements and communications (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter. This Agreement may only be modified, or any rights under it waived, by a written document executed by both Parties.

10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have duly executed this Agreement as of the date first above written.

Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity, so we have added HDI's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Site and HDI's services, breaches of law, data/Confidential Information incidents caused by HDI and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard notice, control and cooperation procedure. Our reciprocal indemnity is deliberately limited to the Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law; if HDI needs relief, we can discuss customary IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations and specifications) and remedies rather than deleting the indemnity.

9A. Indemnification.

9A.1 HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Site or any services, software, tools, materials or deliverables provided by HDI hereunder infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right (other than Content or Marks provided by the Company); (b) HDI's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations; (c) any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure of Confidential Information, Content or customer or user data caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

9A.2 The Company shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless HDI from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Content or Marks provided by the Company infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; or (b) the Company's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations.

9A.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnification is sought, the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim (provided that no settlement that imposes any liability or obligation on, or requires any admission by, the indemnified Party shall be made without its prior written consent), and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate in the defense with counsel of its own choosing at its own expense. This Section 9A shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

9A.2 The Company shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless HDI from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Content or Marks provided by the Company infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; or (b) the Company's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations.

This Section 9A shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.

No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.

Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.

Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

content.text: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-poaching restriction appears anywhere in the agreement. Searches for "solicit," "hire," "induce," "recruit," and "personnel" return nothing relevant, and the only "employee" references are in the confidentiality exception (p0051) and the no-joint-venture clause (p0061). The restrictive covenants that do exist (Section 6 Exclusivity) are product/market non-competes, not personnel restrictions, and fall outside this rule.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Full-text searches for "solicit", "employ or engage", "hire", "induce", "recruit", and "personnel" returned no restrictive personnel covenant; the only employee-related references are the confidentiality carve-out (p0051) and the no-joint-venture/independent-contractor clause (p0061), neither of which restricts hiring. Section 5.4, the only personnel-facing provision, simply requires each Party to appoint a General Manager as liaison. Section 6 (Exclusivity) imposes product/market non-competes rather than personnel restrictions and is outside this rule's scope. This matches our preferred position of no non-solicit on the Customer, so no redline is required.

input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes a field-of-use/non-compete covenant on the Company (our party), barring participation in any project "similar to the Site" not only for Deerskin Products but for open-ended categories of "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and products of unnamed "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled". That undefined scope reaches our broader merchandising business and offers no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions, contrary to our position that we accept no restriction on the businesses we operate or products we buy or build. (The parallel covenant in Section 6.3 binds HDI and is acceptable; Section 6.2 preserves only a narrow closeout carve-out.) Because HDI bears all development and hosting costs for a dedicated "Deerskin" site, we applied the fallback rather than deletion: the restriction is limited to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, for the term only, with carve-outs for other channels, product development and M&A.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, leaving both Parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages; we have added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees or USD 1,000,000 with a mutual exclusion of indirect damages. Confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and the Company's payment obligations under Section 3 are not treated as capped damages; we can accept a straight 12-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct as a fallback.

ops.text: 9(c) Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000), and neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligation to make payments under Section 3 shall not be considered damages subject to the foregoing limitation.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification, defence or hold-harmless provision anywhere (searches for "indemnif" and "hold harmless" return nothing; the outline runs from Warranties (Section 9) straight into General Provisions (Section 10)). HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and its software and tools, so we bear uncovered exposure for third-party IP infringement claims arising from HDI's deliverables, HDI's breaches of law, data/Confidential Information incidents caused by HDI, and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Per the playbook preferred position, we insert a Vendor indemnity after the warranty section with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and keep our reciprocal indemnity narrow (limited to the Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law), with an express survival statement because existing Section 10.7 survival does not reach the new section.

Our reciprocal indemnity is deliberately limited to the Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law; if HDI needs relief, we can discuss customary IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations and specifications) and remedies rather than deleting the indemnity.

9A. Indemnification.

9A.1 HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Site or any services, software, tools, materials or deliverables provided by HDI hereunder infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right (other than Content or Marks provided by the Company); (b) HDI's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations; (c) any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure of Confidential Information, Content or customer or user data caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

9A.2 The Company shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless HDI from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Content or Marks provided by the Company infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; or (b) the Company's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations.

9A.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnification is sought, the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim (provided that no settlement that imposes any liability or obligation on, or requires any admission by, the indemnified Party shall be made without its prior written consent), and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate in the defense with counsel of its own choosing at its own expense. This Section 9A shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

9A. Indemnification.

9A.1 HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Site or any services, software, tools, materials or deliverables provided by HDI hereunder infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right (other than Content or Marks provided by the Company); (b) HDI's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations; (c) any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure of Confidential Information, Content or customer or user data caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

9A.2 The Company shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless HDI from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Content or Marks provided by the Company infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; or (b) the Company's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations.

9A.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnification is sought, the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim (provided that no settlement that imposes any liability or obligation on, or requires any admission by, the indemnified Party shall be made without its prior written consent), and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate in the defense with counsel of its own choosing at its own expense. This Section 9A shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching obligation on The Deerskin Companies (or on HDI). This matches our preferred playbook position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no edit is warranted. If HDI later proposes adding one, our fallback is a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no "no-hire."

Two adjacent points worth noting for the broader review (outside this rule): Section 6.1 imposes a term-length market exclusivity on the Company, and Section 6.3 imposes a two-year post-term restriction on HDI — those are product/market non-competes and should be assessed under the non-compete rule rather than here.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding the Company (our client). Full-text searches for "solicit", "employ or engage", "hire", "induce", "recruit", and "personnel" returned no restrictive personnel covenant; the only employee-related references are the confidentiality carve-out (p0051) and the no-joint-venture/independent-contractor clause (p0061), neither of which restricts hiring. Section 5.4, the only personnel-facing provision, simply requires each Party to appoint a General Manager as liaison. Section 6 (Exclusivity) imposes product/market non-competes rather than personnel restrictions and is outside this rule's scope. This matches our preferred position of no non-solicit on the Customer, so no redline is required.

**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) at Section 6.1 (p0037).**

- **Issue:** Section 6.1 binds *us* (the Company) not to "participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet" with respect to Deerskin Products *or* "products substantially similar" *or* products of unnamed "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" — an undefined field-of-use restriction on our own merchandising business, with no carve-out for product development or acquisitions.
- **Direction check:** The mirror covenant in Section 6.3 binds HDI (and runs two years post-term) — acceptable, left untouched. Section 6.2's closeout carve-out is preserved.

The redline narrows the covenant to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, term-only, with express carve-outs for other channels (catalogs, retail, marketplaces), product development/sourcing, and M&A — while leaving HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right for the Site intact.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 6.1 imposes a field-of-use/non-compete covenant on the Company (our party), barring participation in any project "similar to the Site" not only for Deerskin Products but for open-ended categories of "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and products of unnamed "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled". That undefined scope reaches our broader merchandising business and offers no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions, contrary to our position that we accept no restriction on the businesses we operate or products we buy or build. (The parallel covenant in Section 6.3 binds HDI and is acceptable; Section 6.2 preserves only a narrow closeout carve-out.) Because HDI bears all development and hosting costs for a dedicated "Deerskin" site, we applied the fallback rather than deletion: the restriction is limited to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, for the term only, with carve-outs for other channels, product development and M&A.

Original paragraphs:
p0037: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.

(the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".
Deerskin Products: 1.1 HDI shall design, develop, implement, operate, maintain and manage, and enable the Company to establish a presence on the World Wide Web ("Site") to make available to Internet users on demand, men's and women's apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog ("Deerskin Products"). As used in this Agreement, "Deerskin Products" shall not include (i) closeout merchandise which the Company may identify as "Deerskin" branded items, if such is the case, nor (ii) products from the Company's Joan Cook Catalog.

Rendered redline:
p0037: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not itself establish or operate a self-contained, "Deerskin"-branded web site offering Deerskin Products directly to consumers on the Internet (provided that nothing in this Section 6.1 shall restrict the Company from (i) offering Deerskin Products or any other products through any other channel, including its catalogs, retail stores and third-party marketplaces, (ii) developing, sourcing, marketing or selling any products, or (iii) acquiring, being acquired by, merging with or owning any person engaged in any business, and this Section 6.1 shall not apply following the expiration or termination of this Agreement) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.

The open-ended sweep covering "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" would restrain our broader business, while HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for the Site is preserved.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: MISSING (critical)**

The Site Development and Hosting Agreement has **no indemnification provision at all** — searches for "indemnif" and "hold harmless" returned zero hits, and the document runs directly from Section 9 (Warranties) to Section 10 (General Provisions).

This is a significant exposure for us: HDI designs, develops, hosts, operates and maintains the Site on its own server, using its own software and Content administration tools (§§ 1.1–1.4), yet bears no obligation to defend us against third-party IP infringement claims arising from those deliverables, its breaches of law, data incidents, or its own gross negligence/wilful misconduct.

**Redline inserted** (validated `ok:true`) as new Section 9A after the Warranties section:
- **9A.1** — HDI defends/indemnifies us and our affiliates for third-party IP claims relating to the Site and HDI's services/software/tools, HDI's breach of law, unauthorised access to Confidential Information/Content/user data caused by HDI, and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
- **9A.2** — Our reciprocal indemnity kept deliberately narrow: only the Content and Marks we supply, plus our own breach of law.
- **9A.3** — Standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, with consent required for settlements binding the indemnified party, plus an express survival statement (existing § 10.7 survival lists Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 and would not otherwise capture the new section).

Numbering used "9A" to avoid cascading renumbering of Section 10's eight subsections and the § 10.7 survival cross-reference. If HDI pushes back, the sensible fallback is customary IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies — not deletion of the indemnity.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no indemnification, defence or hold-harmless provision anywhere (searches for "indemnif" and "hold harmless" return nothing; the outline runs from Warranties (Section 9) straight into General Provisions (Section 10)). HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and its software and tools, so we bear uncovered exposure for third-party IP infringement claims arising from HDI's deliverables, HDI's breaches of law, data/Confidential Information incidents caused by HDI, and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Per the playbook preferred position, we insert a Vendor indemnity after the warranty section with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and keep our reciprocal indemnity narrow (limited to the Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law), with an express survival statement because existing Section 10.7 survival does not reach the new section.

9A.1 HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Site or any services, software, tools, materials or deliverables provided by HDI hereunder infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right (other than Content or Marks provided by the Company); (b) HDI's breach of applicable law, rules or regulations; (c) any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure of Confidential Information, Content or customer or user data caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching obligation on The Deerskin Companies (or on HDI). This matches our preferred playbook position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no edit is warranted. If HDI later proposes adding one, our fallback is a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no "no-hire."

Two adjacent points worth noting for the broader review (outside this rule): Section 6.1 imposes a term-length market exclusivity on the Company, and Section 6.3 imposes a two-year post-term restriction on HDI — those are product/market non-competes and should be assessed under the non-compete rule rather than here.

**Finding: MISSING (critical)** — no limitation of liability anywhere in the Agreement.

**Investigation**
- The outline is short (development/hosting terms, exclusivity, cross-promotions, confidentiality, warranties, general provisions). Searches for "liability", "damages" and "indemnif" surfaced no cap or exclusion language — the only "liability" hits are the no-joint-venture disclaimers in §10.2.
- §9 (Warranties) contains only corporate authority reps and a Globix carve-out; §10 (General Provisions) is silent on liability. Result: both Parties are exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages.
- Fee basis checked: §3.1 pays HDI 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month — a real, recurring revenue stream, so a 12-month fee cap is meaningful rather than illusory, but the $1,000,000 floor protects us where sales are low.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — new §9(c) inserted after p0058:
- Mutual cap at the greater of (a) amounts paid or payable by the Company to HDI under §3 in the preceding 12 months and (b) USD 1,000,000.
- Mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential/punitive damages.
- Uncapped "Excluded Claims": confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP.
- The Company's §3 payment obligations are expressly not "damages" subject to the cap.

Placement note: siting the clause in §9 rather than §10 is deliberate — §10.7 already gives Sections 9 and 10 a two-year survival, so the cap and carve-outs survive termination without a further edit to the survival provision.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no limitation-of-liability, aggregate-liability or exclusion-of-damages provision anywhere: searches for "liability" return only the no-joint-venture language (p0061-p0062), and there is no "damages", indemnity or cap language. Section 9 (Warranties, p0055-p0058) and Section 10 (General Provisions) are silent on liability, so both Parties are exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages. We therefore insert a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees payable under Section 3 or USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with the Company's Section 3 payment obligations excluded from the cap. Placement in Section 9 also captures the two-year survival under Section 10.7.

p0058: (b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, restrictive covenants).**

**What I found.** The planner flagged sec-1.4 as the likely location and suspected the rule was absent, but the hosting/services article contains no sole-source language. The real exclusivity sits in Article 6 (paragraph p0037, within sec-5.4): Section 6.1 bars *us* — the Company — from participating in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and gives HDI the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site.

**Why it's a deviation.** Two problems:
- It runs for "the term of this Agreement," and Section 4.1 (p0024) renews the term automatically each year unless terminated — so the restraint is effectively open-ended.
- There is no performance-based exit, even though HDI has hard obligations on site launch and distribution (Sections 1.6, 1.7). That combination is the rule's walk-away scenario.

**Direction check.** I deliberately left alone the provisions that run in our favour: Section 6.2 (our closeout-merchandise carve-out), Section 6.3 (p0042, HDI restricted for two years post-term), and Section 5.2's "exclusive artistic and editorial control," which benefits us. The trademark licence in Section 6.1's second paragraph is already non-exclusive.

**Position taken — fallback, not preferred.** Preferred would be deleting the obligation outright, but that looked disproportionate here: HDI bears all Site design, hosting and promotion costs and gives a reciprocal two-year covenant, so Section 6.1 is part of a genuine mutual bargain. The product scope is also already confined to a defined category. My two-part edit therefore (i) caps the restraint at twelve months from the Effective Date, defining an "Exclusivity Period," and (ii) makes it terminate automatically if HDI misses any service level, availability or delivery date requirement, citing Sections 1.6 and 1.7.

Redline validated `ok:true` before submission. One caveat worth your judgement: I anchored the exit to "service level, availability or delivery date requirements" generically because the agreement has no dedicated SLA section — if you want a tighter trigger, Sections 1.6 and 1.7 could be made the exclusive hooks.

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 6.1 imposes exclusivity on us (the Company/Customer): we may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer web site. This runs for "the term of this Agreement," which under Section 4.1 renews automatically each year, so it is effectively open-ended exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit — the walk-away scenario under the rule. HDI's own restriction in Section 6.3 and the closeout carve-out in Section 6.2 benefit us and are left untouched. Because HDI bears all Site costs and gives a reciprocal two-year covenant, we took the fallback rather than deleting Section 6.1: the restriction is already confined to a defined product category (Deerskin Products), and we added a twelve-month cap plus automatic termination if HDI misses its service level, availability or delivery date obligations (e.g., Sections 1.6 and 1.7).

Original paragraphs:
p0037: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
p0024: 4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. **Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

The document contains no most-favoured-nation mechanic in either direction:

- **Article 3 (Fees; Payment)** is the only commercial-terms article. Section 3.1 fixes a flat 30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold; Sections 3.2–3.4 cover payment timing, quarterly reconciliation and HDI's audit right (at HDI's own cost). Nothing obliges the Company to extend to HDI any better pricing or terms granted to third parties, and nothing requires us to match a third-party offer.
- Targeted searches for *most favored*, *no less favorable*, *favorable*, *price*, *discount*, *match* and *refusal* returned no hits.
- **Section 6.1 (Exclusivity)** does restrain the Company from similar internet projects for Deerskin Products and grants HDI exclusive use of the "Deerskin" brand for a consumer web site, but that is a scope/exclusivity restraint, not an obligation to give HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others — so it falls outside this rule (it may warrant attention under an exclusivity rule instead).

This matches the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no edit is warranted.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation mechanic in either direction. The only commercial terms are the fixed revenue-share and payment mechanics in Article 3 (Sections 3.1-3.4), which set a flat 30% of Net Sales above a monthly threshold with no obligation on the Company to extend to HDI any better pricing, rates or terms granted to third parties, and no obligation to match third-party offers. Searches for "most favored", "no less favorable", "favorable", "price", "discount", "match" and "refusal" returned nothing. The Exclusivity provision (Section 6.1) restricts the Company from participating in similar internet projects for Deerskin Products, but that is a scope/exclusivity restraint rather than an MFN obligation to give HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others, so it is outside this rule. Consistent with the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), no redline is required.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds the Company (our client) anywhere in this Agreement, so our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is warranted. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ or engage", "induce", "recruit", and "personnel" returned no personnel-restrictive covenant. The only employee-related text is the confidentiality carve-out (p0051) and the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause (p0061), neither of which restricts hiring; Section 5.4 (p0035), the sole personnel-facing provision and the planner's candidate location, merely requires each Party to appoint a General Manager as liaison. The survival clause (p0068) lists only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 as surviving, and the entire-agreement clause (p0069) makes this the complete and exclusive agreement, confirming no personnel covenant survives termination or sits outside the four corners. The deterministic checks for a 12-month duration cap and a general-solicitation carve-out are inapplicable: there is no non-solicit clause to constrain, and their failure reflects absence rather than a defect. Section 6 (Exclusivity) imposes product/market non-competes on the Company (6.1) and HDI (6.3) and is outside the scope of this personnel-covenant rule. Should HDI later propose a non-solicit, our fallback is a mutual obligation limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no "no-hire".

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment

Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching obligation on The Deerskin Companies (or on HDI). This matches our preferred playbook position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no edit is warranted. If HDI later proposes adding one, our fallback is a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no "no-hire."

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.
