paragraphs.text: 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

General Manager of its own to act as liaison with the other Party for the Site (each a "General Manager") who shall bear sole responsibility for bookkeeping and business operations of the Site on a day-today basis. Each General Manager shall have the authority to make and convey decisions on behalf of each Party and to be the liaison with the other Party for all production and Content matters.
6. Exclusivity.

6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
The Company hereby grants to HDI a non-exclusive, limited, non-transferable license to use the Company's "Deerskin" trademarks, service

marks, and logos (collectively, "Marks") solely for the purpose of carrying out its obligations under this Agreement. Except as provided herein, no licenses of the Company's Marks are granted or implied under this Agreement.
6.2 The Company retains the right to establish a web site on the Internet for the purpose of offering closeout
merchandise which may be identified as "Deerskin" branded products, if such is the case.

6.3 During the term of this Agreement and for a period of two years after the expiration date of this Agreement, HDI shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet from which products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) are offered for sale to consumers on the Internet.
7. Cross-Promotions.

7.1 Joint Efforts. The Parties agree to cross-promote one another's products through the use of their respective customer e-mail lists on a reciprocal and equitable basis. The Parties specifically agree that the form, content and design of any and all advertisements or promotional materials featuring the other Party or such Party's products shall continue to be developed by or on behalf of such Party and shall be subject to such Party's final approval. The Parties agree further that any promotions or advertisements involving the use of a Party's customer e-mail list by the other Party shall be subject to the prior approval of such Party.

7.2 Mutual Covenants as to Advertisements. The Parties hereby covenant and agree that their respective marketing and advertising efforts provided for herein shall at all times comply with all applicable laws rules and regulations and will

not contain any material which is obscene, threatening, fraudulent, harassing, libelous, infringing of third party intellectual property rights, otherwise illegal or, in the reasonable judgment of the Party required to display or transmit the advertisement, offensive.
8. Confidentiality.

8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the Company, HDI shall maintain the strict confidentiality and shall not disclose to any third party the existence of, or terms and conditions of this Agreement. In addition, HDI, in performing the Services for the Company hereunder, may have access to or be exposed to, directly or indirectly, Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information of the Company in oral, graphic, written, electronic or machine readable form (hereinafter collectively referred to as "Confidential Information"). Confidential Information shall not include information which can be demonstrated:
(a) to have been rightfully in the possession of HDI from a source other than the Company prior to the time of disclosure of said information to HDI hereunder ("Time of Receipt");
(b) to have been in the public domain prior to the Time of Receipt;

(c) to have become part of the public domain after the Time of Receipt by a publication or by any other means except an unauthorized act or omission or breach of this Agreement on the part of HDI, its employees, or agents; or (d) to have been supplied to HDI after the Time of Receipt by a third party who is under no obligation to the
Company to maintain such information in confidence.

8.2 HDI Obligations. All Confidential Information of the Company shall be held in strict confidence by HDI and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of the Company, except as may be required by law. HDI shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for Confidential Information, including measures at least as strict as those HDI uses to protect its own Confidential Information.

8.3 Company's Obligations. The Company acknowledges that it may receive confidential information of HDI relating to its technical, marketing, product and/or business affairs. All such confidential information of HDI shall be-held in strict confidence by the Company and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of HDI, except as may be required by law. The Company shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for such confidential information of HDI, including measures at least as strict as those the Company uses to protect its own Confidential Information.
9. Warranties.

(a) Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation; (2) it has the full right power and authority to enter into, and to perform the obligations contemplated in this Agreement, and the person signing on its behalf has the full right,

power and authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of the Party; (3) this Agreement constitutes a legal valid and binding obligation of the Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; and (4) the execution of this Agreement will not conflict in any way with any pre-existing agreements or understandings of the Party with any person or entity.

(b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date
10. General Provisions.

10.1 Notices. Any notice under this Agreement will be in writing and delivered by personal delivery, express courier, confirmed facsimile, or certified or registered mail, return receipt requested and will be deemed given upon personal delivery, one (1) day after deposit with express courier, upon confirmation of receipt of facsimile or five (5),days after deposit in the mail. Notices will be sent to a Party at its address set forth above or such other address as that Party may specify in writing pursuant to this Section.

10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative. Neither Party shall have any right, power or authority to enter into any agreement for or on behalf of, or to assume or create any obligation, liability, or responsibility on behalf of the other.

This Agreement will not be construed to create or imply an association, joint venture, co-ownership, or partnership between the Parties or to impose any partnership obligation or liability upon either Party.

10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.

10.4 Waiver of Breach. The failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Agreement shall not be deemed or construed to be a waiver of any such provisions, or in any way to affect the right of any Party hereto to thereafter enforce each and every provision of this Agreement. No waiver of any breach of any provisions of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in writing and executed by the Party against which enforcement of such waiver is sought; and no waiver of any such breach shall be construed or deemed to be a waiver of any other or subsequent breach.

10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
10.6 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is declared invalid or otherwise determined to be unenforceable
for any reason, such provision shall be deemed to be severable from the remaining provisions of this Agreement, which shall otherwise remain in full force and effect.
10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

10.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement is the complete and exclusive agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding any prior agreements and communications (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter. This Agreement may only be modified, or any rights under it waived, by a written document executed by both Parties.

10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have duly executed this Agreement as of the date first above written.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site, the URL and the hosting and operation thereof to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content and all customer, user, order and other data relating to the Site or the Deerskin Products, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit-assistance, data-return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "return" and "Content" turn up only notice mechanics, delivery of Content to HDI, and confidentiality). This is a hosting/site-development arrangement in which HDI holds our Content and the Site's customer, user and order data (see p0009, p0016, p0048), so on termination we would have no contractual right to get our data back or to migrate the Site. Under the TRANSITION rule this absence is a deviation requiring an insert. The proposed new Section 4.3 after p0029 gives up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and Site data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification, plus express survival (Section 10.7 at p0068 does not list Section 4). Fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

The Parties specifically agree that the form, content and design of any and all advertisements or promotional materials featuring the other Party or such Party's products shall continue to be developed by or on behalf of such Party and shall be subject to such Party's final approval. The Parties agree further that any promotions or advertisements involving the use of a Party's customer e-mail list by the other Party shall be subject to the prior approval of such Party."},{"id":"p0045","text":"7.2 Mutual Covenants as to Advertisements. The Parties hereby covenant and agree that their respective marketing and advertising efforts provided for herein shall at all times comply with all applicable laws rules and regulations and will"},{"id":"p0046","text":"not contain any material which is obscene, threatening, fraudulent, harassing, libelous, infringing of third party intellectual property rights, otherwise illegal or, in the reasonable judgment of the Party required to display or transmit the advertisement, offensive."},{"id":"p0047","text":"8. Confidentiality."},{"id":"p0048","text":"8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the Company, HDI shall maintain the strict confidentiality and shall not disclose to any third party the existence of, or terms and conditions of this Agreement. In addition, HDI, in performing the Services for the Company hereunder, may have access to or be exposed to, directly or indirectly, Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information of the Company in oral, graphic, written, electronic or machine readable form (hereinafter collectively referred to as \"Confidential Information\"). Confidential Information shall not include information which can be demonstrated:"},{"id":"p0049","text":"(a) to have been rightfully in the possession of HDI from a source other than the Company prior to the time of disclosure of said information to HDI hereunder (\"Time of Receipt\");"},{"id":"p0050","text":"(b) to have been in the public domain prior to the Time of Receipt;"},{"id":"p0051","text":"(c) to have become part of the public domain after the Time of Receipt by a publication or by any other means except an unauthorized act or omission or breach of this Agreement on the part of HDI, its employees, or agents; or (d) to have been supplied to HDI after the Time of Receipt by a third party who is under no obligation to the"},{"id":"p0052","text":"Company to maintain such information in confidence."},{"id":"p0053","text":"8.2 HDI Obligations. All Confidential Information of the Company shall be held in strict confidence by HDI and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of the Company, except as may be required by law. HDI shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for Confidential Information, including measures at least as strict as those HDI uses to protect its own Confidential Information."},{"id":"p0054","text":"8.3 Company's Obligations. The Company acknowledges that it may receive confidential information of HDI relating to its technical, marketing, product and/or business affairs. All such confidential information of HDI shall be-held in strict confidence by the Company and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of HDI, except as may be required by law. The Company shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for such confidential information of HDI, including measures at least as strict as those the Company uses to protect its own Confidential Information."},{"id":"p0055","text":"9. Warranties."},{"id":"p0056","text":"(a) Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation; (2) it has the full right power and authority to enter into, and to perform the obligations contemplated in this Agreement, and the person signing on its behalf has the full right,"},{"id":"p0057","text":"power and authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of the Party; (3) this Agreement constitutes a legal valid and binding obligation of the Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; and (4) the execution of this Agreement will not conflict in any way with any pre-existing agreements or understandings of the Party with any person or entity."},{"id":"p0058","text":"(b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the \"Globix Agreement\") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date"},{"id":"p0059","text":"10. General Provisions."},{"id":"p0060","text":"10.1 Notices. Any notice under this Agreement will be in writing and delivered by personal delivery, express courier, confirmed facsimile, or certified or registered mail, return receipt requested and will be deemed given upon personal delivery, one (1) day after deposit with express courier, upon confirmation of receipt of facsimile or five (5),days after deposit in the mail. Notices will be sent to a Party at its address set forth above or such other address as that Party may specify in writing pursuant to this Section."},{"id":"p0061","text":"10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative. Neither Party shall have any right, power or authority to enter into any agreement for or on behalf of, or to assume or create any obligation, liability, or responsibility on behalf of the other."},{"id":"p0062","text":"This Agreement will not be construed to create or imply an association, joint venture, co-ownership, or partnership between the Parties or to impose any partnership obligation or liability upon either Party."},{"id":"p0063","text":"10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement."},{"id":"p0064","text":"10.4 Waiver of Breach. The failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Agreement shall not be deemed or construed to be a waiver of any such provisions, or in any way to affect the right of any Party hereto to thereafter enforce each and every provision of this Agreement. No waiver of any breach of any provisions of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in writing and executed by the Party against which enforcement of such waiver is sought; and no waiver of any such breach shall be construed or deemed to be a waiver of any other or subsequent breach."},{"id":"p0065","text":"10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws."},{"id":"p0066","text":"10.6 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is declared invalid or otherwise determined to be unenforceable"},{"id":"p0067","text":"for any reason, such provision shall be deemed to be severable from the remaining provisions of this Agreement, which shall otherwise remain in full force and effect."},{"id":"p0068","text":"10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement."},{"id":"p0069","text":"10.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement is the complete and exclusive agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding any prior agreements and communications (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter. This Agreement may only be modified, or any rights under it waived, by a written document executed by both Parties."},{"id":"p0070","text":"10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument."},{"id":"p0071","text":"IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have duly executed this Agreement as of the date first above written."}]}

input.comment: [Playbook] The termination section has no exit provisions, so we have added Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our Content and customer/order data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and then delete and certify deletion. We can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback, but we cannot leave our data and the Site with no return or migration path on exit.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site, the URL and the hosting and operation thereof to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content and all customer, user, order and other data relating to the Site or the Deerskin Products, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit-assistance, data-return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "return" and "Content" turn up only notice mechanics, delivery of Content to HDI, and confidentiality). This is a hosting/site-development arrangement in which HDI holds our Content and the Site's customer, user and order data (see p0009, p0016, p0048), so on termination we would have no contractual right to get our data back or to migrate the Site. Under the TRANSITION rule this absence is a deviation requiring an insert. The proposed new Section 4.3 after p0029 gives up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and Site data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification, plus express survival (Section 10.7 at p0068 does not list Section 4). Fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six months of transition assistance, return Company Content and customer data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certify deletion.
input.comment: [Playbook] The termination section has no exit provisions, so we have added Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our Content and customer/order data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and then delete and certify deletion. We can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback, but we cannot leave our data and the Site with no return or migration path on exit.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site, the URL and the hosting and operation thereof to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content and all customer, user, order and other data relating to the Site or the Deerskin Products, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit-assistance, data-return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "return" and "Content" turn up only notice mechanics, delivery of Content to HDI, and confidentiality). This is a hosting/site-development arrangement in which HDI holds our Content and the Site's customer, user and order data (see p0009, p0016, p0048), so on termination we would have no contractual right to get our data back or to migrate the Site. Under the TRANSITION rule this absence is a deviation requiring an insert. The proposed new Section 4.3 after p0029 gives up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and Site data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification, plus express survival (Section 10.7 at p0068 does not list Section 4). Fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit-assistance, data-return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "return" and "Content" surface only notice mechanics, delivery of Content to HDI, and confidentiality). This is a hosting/site-development arrangement in which HDI holds our Content and the Site's customer, user and order data (p0009, p0016, p0048), so on termination we would have no contractual right to recover our data or migrate the Site. Under the TRANSITION rule this absence is a deviation requiring an insert. The proposed new Section 4.3 after p0029 gives up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and Site data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification, plus express survival (Section 10.7 at p0068 does not list Section 4). Fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

Original paragraphs:
p0023: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
p0024: 4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
p0029: (c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.
p0068: 10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

Resolved definitions:
Company: This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".
Termination Date: 4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").

Rendered redline:
p0029: (c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.
4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site, the URL and the hosting and operation thereof to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content and all customer, user, order and other data relating to the Site or the Deerskin Products, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

Comment:
[Playbook] The termination section has no exit provisions, so we have added Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our Content and customer/order data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and then delete and certify deletion. We can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback, but we cannot leave our data and the Site with no return or migration path on exit.

Document: EXHIBIT 10.2

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-aaf7f213","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement contains no indemnification, defence or hold-harmless provision anywhere (searches for "indemnif" and "hold harmless" return nothing; the outline runs from Warranties (Section 9) straight into General Provisions (Section 10)). HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and its software and tools, so we bear uncovered exposure for third-party IP infringement claims arising from HDI's deliverables, HDI's breaches of law, data/Confidential Information incidents caused by HDI, and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Per the playbook preferred position, we insert a Vendor indemnity after the warranty section with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and keep our reciprocal indemnity narrow (limited to the Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law), with an express survival statement because existing Section 10.7 survival does not reach the new section.","proposal":"Insert mutual indemnification section (HDI IP/misconduct indemnity; narrow Company indemnity) after the Warranties section","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-23b05cc4","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The Agreement contains no intellectual property ownership or assignment provision. HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site and receives all of the Company's Content, Marks and user information (Sections 1.1-1.4, 2.1, 8.1), and the Parties exchange customer e-mail lists (Section 7.1), yet nothing states who owns the Site deliverables, the Content or the customer and order data generated through the Site. The only related language is the negative covenant against co-ownership in Section 10.2, which addresses the corporate relationship rather than IP. Without an express clause we risk HDI asserting ownership of the Site deliverables it develops and of Site customer data. We therefore add a new Section 5.5 confirming Company ownership of Content, Deerskin Products materials and Site deliverables (with HDI assigning), HDI's retention of its pre-existing platform and tools subject to a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back of any HDI IP embedded in the deliverables, exclusive Company ownership of Site customer/order data with a return obligation, and no joint ownership.","proposal":"Add ownership section: Company owns Content, Site deliverables and Site customer data; HDI keeps its platform but licenses embedded IP; no joint ownership.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-0e6116f8","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement contains no limitation-of-liability, aggregate-liability or exclusion-of-damages provision anywhere: searches for "liability" return only the no-joint-venture language (p0061-p0062), and there is no "damages", indemnity or cap language. Section 9 (Warranties, p0055-p0058) and Section 10 (General Provisions) are silent on liability, so both Parties are exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages. We therefore insert a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees payable under Section 3 or USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with the Company's Section 3 payment obligations excluded from the cap. Placement in Section 9 also captures the two-year survival under Section 10.7.","proposal":"Add mutual liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000), mutual consequential-damages exclusion and uncapped Excluded Claims carve-outs","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-02ea966e","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause: it is silent on consent standards, so it neither expressly confirms our right to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets, nor restricts HDI from assigning the development and hosting obligations, including to a competitor of ours. No change-of-control provision appears anywhere in the Agreement, and termination (Sections 2/2.x, p0024–p0026) is notice-based, so there is no Vendor exit or re-pricing trigger on our change of control (no walk-away issue). The gap is the missing asymmetric allocation required by the preferred position, so we add the Customer affiliate/successor carve-out, a consent requirement (not unreasonably withheld) with a no-competitor limit on HDI's assignment, and express confirmation that our change of control is not an assignment and gives HDI no termination or re-pricing right.","proposal":"Add Customer affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, consent restriction on HDI's assignment (no competitors), and confirm no HDI rights on Company change of control.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-0192b78e","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 imposes exclusivity on us (the Company/Customer): we may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer web site. This runs for "the term of this Agreement," which under Section 4.1 renews automatically each year, so it is effectively open-ended exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit — the walk-away scenario under the rule. HDI's own restriction in Section 6.3 and the closeout carve-out in Section 6.2 benefit us and are left untouched. Because HDI bears all Site costs and gives a reciprocal two-year covenant, we took the fallback rather than deleting Section 6.1: the restriction is already confined to a defined product category (Deerskin Products), and we added a twelve-month cap plus automatic termination if HDI misses its service level, availability or delivery date obligations (e.g., Sections 1.6 and 1.7).","proposal":"Cap Section 6.1 exclusivity at 12 months and add automatic termination on HDI performance failure","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-2fc213ac","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.2 imposes a one-way liquidated exit charge payable solely by the Company (our client) whenever it terminates: 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, paid in eight quarterly instalments. HDI never owes a reciprocal amount (4.2(b) expressly confirms it makes no payment even if the formula is negative). The charge is untethered from the fees actually payable (30% of Net Sales over $11,000/month) and is triggered by any Company termination — including the 90-day non-renewal right in 4.1 and termination for HDI's breach — so it can exceed remaining contract value on a one-year rolling term. That contravenes the playbook position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by the Customer. Redline deletes Section 4.2 and conforms the Section 4 heading; the fallback offer is a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees for convenience terminations only.","proposal":"Delete the Company-payable Termination Payment in Section 4.2 and conform the Section 4 heading.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-fe02a09e","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 1.4 is the grant of access/use rights running to us (the Company). It names only "the Company", so our affiliates and the contractors and agents who will actually build, populate and administer the Site are not covered, and administration-tool access is confined to the narrow purpose of monitoring catalog information. The grant is also silent on revocability, leaving HDI room to suspend or withdraw access outside the Section 4 termination mechanics. Successor transfer is already addressed by Section 10.3 (agreement inures to successors and assigns), so no edit is needed there, and the negotiated one-year renewable term with termination payment is left intact rather than converting to a breach-only termination standard. The redline makes the minimal changes: adding affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, broadening tool access to the exercise of our rights, and confirming irrevocability during the term.","proposal":"Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to the Company's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf and make those rights irrevocable during the term (subject only to Section 4 termination).","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-3f600f9a","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 imposes a field-of-use/non-compete covenant on the Company (our party), barring participation in any project "similar to the Site" not only for Deerskin Products but for open-ended categories of "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and products of unnamed "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled". That undefined scope reaches our broader merchandising business and offers no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions, contrary to our position that we accept no restriction on the businesses we operate or products we buy or build. (The parallel covenant in Section 6.3 binds HDI and is acceptable; Section 6.2 preserves only a narrow closeout carve-out.) Because HDI bears all development and hosting costs for a dedicated "Deerskin" site, we applied the fallback rather than deletion: the restriction is limited to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, for the term only, with carve-outs for other channels, product development and M&A.","proposal":"Narrow Section 6.1 exclusivity so the Company is restricted only from operating a competing "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site during the term, with carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-66f3977e","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.1 gives the Company only a 90-day convenience right (and gives HDI a symmetrical right that, on its face, is not confined to the end of a term), while Section 4.2 imposes an uncapped, formula-based Termination Payment on the Company alone equal to 50% of the preceding twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000 — a penalty that can far exceed the 30% revenue-share fees actually payable under Section 3.1 and well above the playbook's 3-months'-fees fallback cap. Playbook position: Customer may exit for convenience on 30 days' notice without penalty and with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and Vendor has no mid-term convenience right. The redline adds the 30-day Company right with refund, restricts HDI's convenience termination to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice, and removes the Termination Payment; the 3-month fee cap fallback is offered in the comment.","proposal":"Give the Company a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund, limit HDI's convenience right to the end of a term, and remove the Net Sales-based Termination Payment.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-8c7da5d6","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint, an audit right binding us does exist: Section 3.4 (p0022) lets HDI inspect the Company's payment-calculation records. It is the only such provision (searches for "inspect"/audit surface nothing else).

Measured against the preferred position, it already satisfies several elements and is not flagged for them: 30 days' prior written notice (meets preferred), inspection during the Company's normal business hours, and HDI bearing all inspection fees unconditionally — better than preferred, which permits cost-shifting on a 5% underpayment. Those terms benefit us and were left untouched.

Two gaps remain. First, frequency is uncapped — HDI could inspect repeatedly, which approaches the walk-away trigger of "unlimited audits." We added a once-per-twelve-month cap. Second, the inspector is HDI's own General Manager with no confidentiality tether specific to the audit and no limit on scope. Section 8.2 (p0053) does oblige HDI to hold Company Confidential Information in strict confidence, so this gap is partly mitigated; we nonetheless made the confidentiality binding explicit and permitted an independent auditor as an alternative.

No remote or direct system-access language exists, so nothing needed deleting; we added a confirmation that the review is records-only to foreclose scope creep into our systems. Severity is medium and the notice/cost bargain is already favourable, hence a narrow single-paragraph edit rather than a rewrite.","proposal":"Cap payment-record inspections at once per 12 months, bind the inspector to confidentiality, and bar access to Company systems.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-7cbd1d19","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 10.5 selects New York law, which is our preferred governing law. However, the Agreement contains no dispute forum provision at all: searches for "jurisdiction", "court", "venue" and "arbitration" return no results, so no exclusive venue is designated (and no foreign arbitration seat is imposed). The preferred position requires exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, so we add that venue language to the existing sentence without disturbing the governing law choice.","proposal":"Add exclusive New York County court venue to the New York governing law clause.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-ae238c76","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation mechanic in either direction. The only commercial terms are the fixed revenue-share and payment mechanics in Article 3 (Sections 3.1-3.4), which set a flat 30% of Net Sales above a monthly threshold with no obligation on the Company to extend to HDI any better pricing, rates or terms granted to third parties, and no obligation to match third-party offers. Searches for "most favored", "no less favorable", "favorable", "price", "discount", "match" and "refusal" returned nothing. The Exclusivity provision (Section 6.1) restricts the Company from participating in similar internet projects for Deerskin Products, but that is a scope/exclusivity restraint rather than an MFN obligation to give HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others, so it is outside this rule. Consistent with the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), no redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-1751aec6","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The only payment obligation on the Company (Section 3, para p0019) is a pure revenue share — 30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 per-month threshold — so fees accrue solely from actual sales generated through the Site. The $11,000 figure is a floor below which nothing is owed (a benefit to us), not a minimum spend. HDI bears the design, development, hosting and promotion costs (paras p0006, p0014), and there is no take-or-pay, minimum purchase, shortfall make-whole, or cap/floor on Company volume anywhere in the text; searches for "minimum", "commit" and "fee" return no commitment language. The term is a single year with rolling one-year renewals terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (para p0024), which satisfies even the fallback exit requirement. Separately, Section 4.2(a) (para p0026) imposes a Termination Payment if the Company terminates, calculated as (trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000) / 2. That is an exit charge measured by actual achieved sales rather than a penalty for failing to hit a committed volume, so it does not create a take-or-pay obligation under this rule; it is priced-exit exposure properly addressed under the termination-fee/early-exit rule rather than redlined here. No edit is warranted for MINCOMMIT.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-04a745d4","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.1 provides evergreen automatic one-year renewals with a 90-day non-renewal notice window. The 12-month renewal term is acceptable, but the 90-day window exceeds both our preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day limits and sits at the walk-away boundary, and there is no vendor reminder before renewal. Fees are revenue-share based on Net Sales with no unilateral uplift mechanism, so no price-increase cap is needed. Redline shortens the window to 30 days and requires HDI to give a renewal reminder 60 days before each anniversary.","proposal":"Shorten non-renewal notice window from 90 to 30 days and add HDI renewal reminder 60 days before each anniversary","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-6ed5cc32","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit-assistance, data-return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "return" and "Content" surface only notice mechanics, delivery of Content to HDI, and confidentiality). This is a hosting/site-development arrangement in which HDI holds our Content and the Site's customer, user and order data (p0009, p0016, p0048), so on termination we would have no contractual right to recover our data or migrate the Site. Under the TRANSITION rule this absence is a deviation requiring an insert. The proposed new Section 4.3 after p0029 gives up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of Content and Site data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification, plus express survival (Section 10.7 at p0068 does not list Section 4). Fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.","proposal":"Insert Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six months of transition assistance, return Company Content and customer data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certify deletion.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-a6248bb3","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only mutual representations as to corporate existence, authority, enforceability and non-conflict (p0056-p0057) plus a Globix carve-out (p0058). There is no express performance warranty from HDI covering the design, development, hosting, operation and maintenance of the Site, no conformance warranty for the Site or software, no compliance-with-law or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/re-performance/refund remedy. (There is also no disclaimer, so nothing swallows an express warranty.) Under the playbook this absence is a deviation requiring insertion; we added a new Section 9(c) with workmanlike services, a 12-month conformance period for the Site/software, legal compliance and no malicious code, with a re-performance, repair/replacement or refund remedy, and flagged the 90-day/30-day fallback.","proposal":"Add an HDI performance warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformance for the Site/software, legal compliance, no malicious code) with a repair/re-perform/refund remedy.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-c9e4fb1b","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement has no insurance article: a search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the General Provisions (Section 10, paragraphs p0059-p0070) run from Notices through Headings/Counterparts with no coverage requirement. HDI is squarely a services/hosting vendor to us: it designs, develops, hosts, operates and maintains the Site on its own server (Sections 1.1, 1.3, 1.4), collects customer orders and processes our inventory data (Section 1.5), and expressly acknowledges access to our "Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information" as Confidential Information (Section 8.1). A vendor that hosts our storefront and processes consumer order and user data with no insurance backstop hits the playbook walk-away position, so we insert the standard coverage package (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) as a new Section 10.9, placed at the end of the General Provisions where it is captured by the Section 10 survival language in Section 10.7. Fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is available if HDI's program cannot reach the preferred limits.","proposal":"Insert a new Section 10.9 requiring HDI to carry commercial general liability, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation insurance, with certificates on request.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-ac5c7341","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"low","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding The Deerskin Companies, so our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already satisfied and no redline is appropriate. **To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review findings and negotiation posture

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2. The Agreement is materially incomplete on risk allocation: it contains **no indemnification, no intellectual property ownership provision, and no limitation of liability** of any kind. 2. **Vendor insurance (§ 10, missing).** A vendor that hosts our storefront and processes consumer order and user data with no insurance backstop hits the playbook walk-away position. Coverage — at minimum the fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M — is required.
